[docs/resource-guides/onprem/custom.md#other-on-premises-services-type-custom]
`custom` covers anything else functions talk to: an SMTP server, LDAP / Active Directory, an internal REST API, an Elasticsearch cluster, a file share. pskit only hands `connection` values to handlers (`external: true` is required). Not to be confused with the **custom driver** (`options.driver: custom`), which plugs your own class into a `queue` or `storage` resource so it can trigger functions: see [queue.md](queue.md#rabbitmq-or-kafka-nats--via-a-custom-driver).

[docs/resource-guides/onprem/queue.md#on-premises-queues-type-queue]
Trigger functions on the host from a queue: the host's built-in queue, Redis / Valkey, RabbitMQ or Kafka through a custom driver, or a queue in a cloud. Every option gives the same at-least-once handling: `batch_size`, `visibility_timeout`, `max_receive`, `dead_letter` and `BatchResult` work the same way.

[docs/resource-guides/onprem/secrets.md#secret-managers-on-premises]
Keep API keys, database passwords and certificates in a secret manager instead of files, and read them from handlers with **one call that works on every provider**: No extra library: the calls are part of the pskit runtime (Python standard library, Node.js built-ins). Values are cached for 60 seconds per function instance.

[docs/resource-guides/onprem/services.md#one-click-services-for-on-premises-functions]
pskit can **create** the queue, stream, bucket, database or cache your on-premises functions use, then add it to `pskit.yml` as a resource and, for queues, streams and buckets, as a trigger. It starts the service as a Docker container on this machine or on any server you can reach with SSH. That can be the server your functions run on or a different one. It can also install Python or Docker on an SSH server.

[docs/resource-guides/onprem/storage.md#on-premises-storage-type-storage]
Run functions when files appear in a bucket, and read or write objects: the host's built-in buckets, a shared folder, MinIO or another S3-compatible store, or a bucket in a cloud (S3, R2, Azure Blob, GCS, ...). The host lists each watched bucket every `poll_seconds` and compares ETags: a new or changed object emits `created`, a missing one `deleted`. Objects already there at the first start are recorded, not emitted.
